unnamed-god.label: Unnamed god
unnamed-god.note: This male relief type is reused for several recipients: an unnamed hostile god, a plague god, a road god and a tutelary deity. Its dress and pose follow the male deities at Yazılıkaya; the texts do not identify those recipients as the same god or prescribe this carving.

unnamed-goddess.label: Unnamed goddess
unnamed-goddess.note: Puliša's ritual leaves the female deity unnamed. The long garment and cylindrical headdress follow the goddess reliefs at Yazılıkaya; this is a visual comparison, not a named cult image.

storm-god.label: Storm-god
storm-god.note: The tablet calls the recipient Storm-god. The relief takes its form from the depiction of Teššub at Yazılıkaya; the tablet does not identify this recipient as Teššub by name.

sun-god.label: Sun-god
sun-god.model: Sun-god of Heaven relief at Yazılıkaya, no. 34
sun-god.note: The round cap, long robe and curved crook follow the Sun-god of Heaven relief at Yazılıkaya. The ritual says Sun-god without that fuller identification.

the-seven.label: The Seven
the-seven.model: Repeated male deity reliefs at Yazılıkaya
the-seven.note: The tablet names the Seven (Sebettu). This seven-figure grouping uses the repeated Hittite relief type as a visual convention; the Yazılıkaya figures are not identified as the Sebettu.

divine-assembly.label: All the gods
divine-assembly.model: Male and female deity processions at Yazılıkaya
divine-assembly.note: The tablet addresses all the gods collectively. The small group draws on the male and female processions at Yazılıkaya; its four figures do not represent a fixed list of recipients.
